name: Brixen im Thale
kurzbeschreibung: Popular family-friendly village in the Wilder Kaiser ski world, featuring the mountain railway and the stunning Badesee.
beschreibung:
Overview

Brixen im Thale is a vibrant and welcoming municipality in the Kitzbühel district, situated at an altitude of approximately 794 meters in the heart of the picturesque Brixen Valley. As the oldest settlement and namesake of the entire valley, the village counts around 2,700 residents across a municipal area of over 31 square kilometers. Framed by the rugged limestone ridges of the Wilder Kaiser to the north and the rolling grass mountains of the Kitzbühel Alps to the south, dominated by Mount Hohe Salve (1,828 m), Brixen pairs authentic Tyrolean village traditions with premier recreational facilities, serving as a year-round hub for mountain and winter sports.

History

Archaeological evidence of settlement dates back to the Bronze Age, as proven by the discovery of a bronze flanged axe that now adorns the municipal coat of arms. The village was first documented between 788 and 790 in the Indiculus Arnonis records of Salzburg Bishop Arn as ad Prixina ecclesia cum territorio. This confirms Brixen as the oldest documented village in the valley, serving as the historical mother parish for all surrounding communities. A revered local tradition is the annual Antlassritt on Corpus Christi, a ceremonial equestrian procession of local farmers from Brixen, Kirchberg, and Westendorf riding to the Swedish Chapel, commemorating the defense against Swedish troops in 1648 during the Thirty Years' War. The imposing Deanery Church of the Assumption of Mary and Saint Martin was erected between 1790 and 1795 in a Late Baroque-Neoclassical transition style, featuring magnificent ceiling frescoes by Joseph Schöpf.

How to Get There

By car, Brixen im Thale is reached via the Inntal motorway A12, taking exit Wörgl-Ost and following federal highway B170 through Hopfgarten in about fifteen minutes; toll-free access from Germany is possible via federal roads from Kufstein. Rail travelers enjoy direct connections along the Salzburg-Tyrol Railway: the Brixen im Thale railway station is served every thirty minutes by the Tyrolean S-Bahn (line S8) and regional REX trains between Wörgl and Kitzbühel. Free winter ski buses connect seamlessly across the valley.

Tips

In winter, the Hochbrixen gondola provides immediate access into the SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser-Brixental, one of the largest and most modern ski networks in the world with over 270 kilometers of pistes. At the mountain station, the ALPENIGLU Village fascinates visitors with intricate ice sculptures, an ice bar, and overnight igloos. In summer, Lake Filzalmsee at 1,300 meters altitude delights families with its giant adventure stations, moor walking pools, and nature biotope. Ascending Mount Hohe Salve rewards hikers with a 360-degree panoramic vista spanning more than seventy glaciated three-thousanders. On the valley floor, the Brixen Leisure Lake offers crystal-clear bathing, giant water slides, and sunbathing lawns.
